utterances.text: You told us -- and I ask you this again because it wasn't reflected in the transcript. The sculptures of the saints, can you tell us what was done to the sculpture of the saints?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: They were broken, heads off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their heads were cut off.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Someone cuts the heads off the statues?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, by some -- I don't know. Broken, destructed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, the approximate time period in 1993 when you were at the Catholic church in Travnik, day or perhaps month.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: It must have been in the second half of May or first day of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive at any point any information as to who had destroyed or damaged the Catholic church in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The person who guided me in the church, it was totally obvious that it was Muslim foreigners or Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: She told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the damage that you observed and witnessed, could you tell what was the cause of that damage?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: What -- no reasonable cause for damage inventory in a church. I can't imagine how people can do such a thing. It's an obvious violation of human rights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the destruction appear to you to be intentional or was it somehow related to any type of combat?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't think there had been some combat in that church, at least, because there were no damages from fightings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you about any houses or homes that you observed in Travnik. Do you recall anything unusual that you saw with respect to houses in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah. Travnik was in my opinion a very difficult area because Travnik was appointed as a capital of the province number ten in the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, and both sides tried to get majority in this province number ten. And that is probably the reason for the heavy fighting there in the first half of June. And one member of the Croat -- Croat member of the municipality board, he had been, as he told me, expelled by Muslim soldiers, and he lived at this time in Bila area, Han Bila, I think it was. And we tried, of course, to reunify Travnik but with no success. And a large part of the Croat people in Travnik disappeared. And I have not got any reasonable explanation why they left. But most reasonable explanation must be that they felt a strong threat from the Muslim side. And on several emptied houses, so to say ex-Croat houses, there were posters or signs put up that said "This property is protected by the Muslim or BiH." I think you have the text of the signs in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember discussing this with anyone?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Of course, we noticed it and discussed within the colleagues, what's the reason for that. They know -- those people who put up these signs, they must have known that the Croats have left. And by some reason, they wanted to keep the houses, perhaps for incoming refugees from other areas or some other reason I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Junhov.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions in direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think it would be best to have the break now. It's quarter to 5.00, and we will resume at quarter past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, you may take the floor for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Bourgon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Junhov.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have had the pleasure and the opportunity to meet a little earlier today. And before I begin, I wish to express my appreciation for you taking the time to meet us. So on behalf of the Defence, thank you very much. I did on this occasion introduce myself but just for the sake of the transcript, let me again introduce myself and the team I am with today. I'm accompanied today by Mrs. Edina Residovic and by Mr. Alexis Demirdjian. And my name is Stephane Bourgon. And together, we represent General Hadzihasanovic. I wish to begin, Mr. Junhov, by simply confirming that you did give a statement to the Office of the Prosecution or to investigators in 1997. Is that correct? Which would be one year before you testified.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: But I testified in 1998, if remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you testified in 1998. Do you recall testifying in 1998?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go step by step. Do you recall testifying and you answered this question to the President, in 1998, and that was in the Aleksovski case? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, Kaonik prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you provided the Office of the Prosecution with a statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is on the occasion where you spent lots of time with the investigator to file the statement.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a further statement in the month of February 2001, which was just a little more than two years ago. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, the events took place more than 11 years ago today, so I fully understand that sometimes it is not possible to remember everything. However, would you confirm for the benefit of the Trial Chamber that even though these events took place more than 11 years ago, today you still have nightmares about the moments and the experience and about everything you saw in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that for you, you take no pleasure in being here today and recalling these events.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: On the contrary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as an ECMM, can you confirm that you had no access to the Army of the Republika Srpska or to what we call the VRS?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. According to our basic documents, we should have unlimited access to all territory. But we were not allowed into the Serb area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for this reason, can you confirm that you focussed all of your attention to the conflict between the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that for this reason, you do not know exactly what was happening on the front line between the Serb Army and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: From inside Central Bosnia so to say, but not from the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew, however, that the army -- the Serb Army was regularly shelling Central Bosnia and shelling the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: They were shelling the territory. I noticed that several times. For instance, just some hours after we heard on the radio a news broadcast about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, there were shellings from the Serb side just out the British Battalion in Vitez. One or two hours later, there were shellings there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are able to confirm that there was indeed lots of shelling from the Serb down in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to the issue that you discussed, and that is of the Kaonik prison which you covered in your testimony in 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the information which led you to go to Kaonik in the first place was received by the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that when you had initially, on the 2nd of April, and that was at the Busovaca Joint Commission, that Mr. Nakic denied having any knowledge of the people detained in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember that exactly. But I think you have it in my written paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I take your statement that you provided in 2001, and if I just quote to you a short line concerning the role, and it says here "I recall Nakic making a comment that he had no knowledge about those foreigners." Do you recall making this statement?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Mr. Nakic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nakic.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And then you visited Kaonik with a colleague of yours, namely, Mr. Schellschmidt?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also confirm that initially, when you found out about Kaonik -- because you did not know, right, that Kaonik existed?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you did find out, you were initially refused access to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That's on the first attempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had to go to the chief of police in Busovaca in order to get permission to have access to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Because the guard there said he was not allowed to let anybody in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then once you did have access, you were dealing with the person you believed to be the commander of Kaonik prison.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, he introduced himself as the commander, or the man responsible for the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that occasion is when you met the five foreigners. Now, earlier in response to a question from my colleague, you said there might have been seven. But if I read from your statement, and it says five, would that be five? Or do you recall if there was five or seven?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I have presented photos of these individuals, so -- they are somewhere in the files there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I have a picture here which maybe I can show you and you can confirm whether these are the individuals that you did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is the photograph that the Defence was provided with, and it was attached to the witness's statement taken in 2001 by investigators from the OTP. It's a black and white photograph, and we don't have the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's me myself who has made this photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] You took this picture yourself?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask, Mr. Junhov, that you simply initial this picture and put a date on it. And I will ask that it be -- that it be introduced in evidence to show the five people that you met.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah. I think on the backside of the photo, there is a note of the date and the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe on the original, but on this one, there is nothing. So I would simply take this sheet of paper, and get you to put your initials and a date, and we will enter it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, as far as tendering this photograph into evidence is concerned, this photograph which is a copy of a black-and-white photograph, what is your position? The witness says that he took this photograph himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the exhibit number will be DH189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] The five individuals -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, but I don't remember exactly the date. You have it in my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I have a date here. But if you just sign it and put today's date that today you recognise this picture as having been taken by yourself during the time you spent in Bosnia, and that day you said you were accompanied by Mr. Schellschmidt. So simply sign and put today's date, please.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Now, earlier on, you answered a question from my colleague that these five foreigners were most likely from Libya, Saudi Arabia and Afghanistan. Now, in your statement here, it says that these people were from Pakistan, Egypt, Tunis, and Algeria.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm or you just did not know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: What is written in my first statement must be most correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are these notes -- did you obtain this information on that day from these people?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you confirm once again that these people informed you that they were missionaries.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. On my question, what are you doing here, the answer was "We are missionaries".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also confirm that the issue of money and that the issue of weapons, both issues were raised during the examination-in-chief, and in your view both of these issues were rumours.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah. I couldn't confirm it because there were no evidence of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you did ask them why they were arrested, do you recall that they told you that they did not know why they had been arrested, but that they had been arrested immediately upon entry in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the answer. But they were arrested and they had no -- as they explained to me, no reason for -- they hadn't been told any reason for their arresting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say that once again, please.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I mentioned before there were a language problem because these people didn't speak English, very bad English. Some of them knew some words in German, French. But on my question, I got the impression that they had not been explained by the Croats why they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I move quickly to your testimony, and that is your testimony that you gave in 1998 concerning the coordination committee meeting. Now, in your testimony, you mention that this meeting took place on the 7th of April. Can you confirm this.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: There were a lot of meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you said so in your testimony, would that be --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- a proper --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that occasion, you also mentioned in your testimony that at the meeting, there was a request for Kaonik prison to be inspected.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that on this occasion, the committee decided that ICRC, the International Committee of the Red Cross, would do the inspection, and they were actually present during that meeting. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: If I have written that, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can just refer you to the testimony itself so that I can be sure that this is what you said and you can confirm. I have your testimony here, and I will refer you to the exact area. It says here: "Was there any discussion about the Kaonik prison at this particular meeting?" And your answer was: "Yes. Amongst all other items on the agenda, there was a request or a demand to get this prison examined." The next question is: "Examined by whom?" And your answer is: "Or inspected." And the question then is: "Examined or inspected by whom?" And then your answer is: "According to a decision in the committee, the task was given to the ICRC."

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just confirm with you, Mr. Junhov, that --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what was the question about that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply to confirm that the decision to have Kaonik prison inspected, there was someone who put a request forward, and the committee decided to give this task to the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my next question is: Do you recall that you mentioned that there was a request for those persons to be transferred to the prison in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you also confirm that, because I've looked at your testimony and both of your statements, and nowhere does it say that there was a request or any indication for these people to be released.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: But there was a general understanding that people who were detained without any juridical reasons, they should be released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So because there was no legal basis, then, it was discussed it should -- if there was no legal basis, they should be released?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, and that was not only the question in Kaonik; it was other places, too, where people were detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, these persons, that's probably the reason why they requested them to be transferred to the real prison in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Might have been. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on to another area, and that is the 20th of April. Now, I would like to refer you to a document. And before I go on, I will give you a series of documents which we will use during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a series of eight documents here. These are documents, the ones that will be used by the Judges and the witness, have been indexed. There are tabs, and we have a sufficient number of copies for everyone present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Junhov, I would like to refer you to tab number 5, which is a special report dated 20 and 21 April. And I would like to refer to the second page in this report where it is indicated that the report was prepared by Mr. Torbjorn --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lars, which would be Mr. Baggesen?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Remy, I guess this would be?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The Canadian monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Landry.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. Remy Landry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to paragraph number 2 where it says "Croat communities in Zenica." If you can read where it says: "The following Zenica Croat suburbs were visited to clarify the housing situation..." And where it says that "it was safe to have their inhabitants return." And there's a series of towns which are mentioned. And where it says that "the local commander, local BiH commander, Nuraga was met, and he confirmed us that he had received strict orders regarding all the vacated houses and villages. He had to patrol to assure their security with the military BiH police, including patrol and creation of joint commissions with the local inhabitants. We were told that every HVO soldier that wanted to return to his village could do it if he surrendered by handing back his personal weapon and assuming that he was not part of the shelling on Zenica. In all of the villages visited, the Croats interviewed mentioned that they had received aid and protection from their Muslim neighbours during the fighting. During one of the visits, we witnessed the capture of criminals who were robbing houses by the special military BiH police." Do you recall this visit and the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I recall the contents of the document, but I wasn't -- I didn't take part in this visit in these villages. That was carried out by Mr. Remi Landry. But we always made these kind of special reports. We picked together from different monitors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the information, and the information was summed up and indicated into this kind of report.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you acknowledge that these issues, these events were discussed with you with your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I would like the usher, please, to bring the Prosecution Exhibit 148, which was referred to earlier on during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, I would like you to confirm, Mr. Junhov, that you yourself never did go to Miletici.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, I was not present there. As I remember it, it was Erik Friis-Pedersen, together with Mr. Merdan and Mr. Nakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you are able to confirm based on this written document that those people who did the killings in Miletici were the Mujahedin, the Arabic-speaking people.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to refer you to this specific document, but to the paragraph just above -- or sorry, the paragraph just later where it talks about the joint operations centre and where it says that there was -- "a decision was made..." I refer you specifically to paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: In which paper?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second page. This is the one -- the Prosecution exhibit you have in paragraph 4 where it says "tripartite meetings" and where it says that "the commission sat today and discussed the cease-fire violations." Now, I refer you to the end of this paragraph where it says: "In the afternoon, it was decided to send an investigation team of the joint operations centre to Miletici." And then it says: "See above, paragraph 2 C." Can you confirm that this paragraph, this decision by the joint operations centre, the decision was to send Mr. Merdan and Mr. Nakic together to go and take a look and confirm rumours they had heard concerning the events in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. Since you have it in the report, it must be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm that this was the proper procedure whereby parties would meet at the joint operations centre, they would discuss issues, and if one or the other or both parties wanted to confirm and to investigate, then there would be a decision made for both parties to travel together and confirm whether any rumours were right or wrong.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That was the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that they would then be accompanied by a member from the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, or from the UNPROFOR or both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this case, it's Mr. Friis-Pedersen.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- who accompanied Mr. Nakic and Mr. Merdan.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And together they went to Miletici and they confirmed the information at paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, it seems so. I don't remember exactly the discussions here, but I take for obvious that the report is reflecting the correct procedures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Junhov.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: This document can be taken back from the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move to another issue, and that is on the 26th of April. And I refer to you the series of documents you have before you, and this is the document at tab number 6. Now, if we look at this document, Mr. Junhov, it says that the main task for the team -- would you agree that this would be the team Z1 which was composed of Mr. Baggesen and Mr. Morsink?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it was to move as much people from Grahovcici back to their homes as soon as possible? And that there was a phase approach --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The reports says it was to remove as much people from -- as possible, not as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. You're absolutely correct. The first sentence says "as possible," to their homes as possible. So as many people as possible, to move them back to their reports.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm according to this report, the transport was arranged by Father Stipan as long as the head of the civil protection of Zenica. Can you confirm, Mr. Junhov, that the civil protection of Zenica is a civil organisation?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I didn't take part in this special event. But generally, as you can see here, obviously it has worked this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just my question to you was can you confirm the existence of the civil protection service of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. There existed some kind of organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was not a military organisation, but a civilian organisation.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't really know. But in my opinion, they had some kind of -- should we call him Lord Mayor of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mayor of Zenica. Do you recall the name of the mayor of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you Mr. Spahic, does that ring a bell to you?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I have heard the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you the name Fazlic as being the chief of police of Zenica, is that something that you recall at all?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I remember I met with the chief of police a couple of times, but there is no bell ringing of the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I show you a picture of the chief of police, would you be able to recall?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Let us have a try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the picture, Mr. Junhov, and tell me if you remember or if you can see who the peoples in this picture are.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. From the right in my view here, the civilian, his role I'm not fully clear if it was a politician or some kind of civilian officer. And then it's Mr. Merdan and Mr. Hadzihasanovic. Then I think it's some interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say the last name again because I missed the --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Hadzihasanovic. The commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Beside Mr. Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Mr. Merdan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, going the other way, the lady.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The lady, I think she was an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then moving down?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That is the Danish monitor. We had his name on a paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Junhov, again, the civilian that you are mentioning --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- do you recognise this gentleman as being Mr. Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Chief of police.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. I think this photo was taken -- it's me who has taken the photo. And I think it was in a meeting in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would ask you that we use the same procedure, Mr. Junhov, and that you put your initials on this picture as well as today's date. And I will ask that it be admitted, of course, under the caveat that you could not recognise the man who is dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I recognise him. I have seen him, of course. But I can't verify the name of him. It might also have been a meeting in BritBat in Vitez. But on the other side of the table, there was the opposite members from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you that this is the picture that was -- that accompanied your statement and that was, of course, taken by yourself and it is indeed the meeting in Kaonik on the 7th of April. Kakanj, sorry.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Kakanj, yeah. Okay. Then we agree. Should I sign it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like these photos to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, may we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH190 will be the next number, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] If I can just refer you to this document that we were looking at tab number 6, and to refer you to later down in the paragraph where it says, and just at paragraph 2, the fifth line -- sorry the fourth line where it begins by "there, we heard that HVO Travnik had ordered to stop all refugees from going back to their houses, and it was said that they were ordered to go to Nova Bila." Do you recall discussing this event with your colleagues Baggesen and Morsink, that the fact that Travnik were basically ordering their people not to return to their villages and instead to go to Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: There was a lot of discussion about the Croats in Travnik. And I can't remember exactly this point here. But there were a lot of discussions how to handle the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that these people from Travnik that you mention, Mr. Junhov, were the HVO from Travnik ordering their people not to return to their houses.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: It stands so here. And the notes -- the report is written by the two monitors who witnessed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you recall these discussions about the HVO in Travnik telling their people not to return to their houses?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No, I can't remember because I was -- obviously I was not present at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I bring you down to a little further down, six lines from the bottom, where it says "the local press" -- just below this sentence, where it says, "It appeared that rumours on massacres in and around Zenica were told by the HVO, probably to scare people from going back to their homes, and the team reported on their experiences of phase 1 and was able to calm the situation. And Father Stipan and reps of the refugees used some time to discuss the matter and explain the situation to all refugees. And the refugees told to be forced back from the checkpoint in Novi Selo to Grahovcici by HVO soldiers firing warning shots in the air." Do you recall the use of propaganda and rumours to scare the people from going back to their houses?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Generally, there was a lot of rumours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this case, do you recall your colleagues discussing with you that they actually had taken three buses which were kind of hijacked by the HVO, and the three HVO, the police and the HVO took the buses away from both of your colleagues and Father Stipan? Do you recall this event being discussed at all?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on to another issue, Mr. Junhov. And that is the -- you mentioned that you had seen a church which had been destroyed by - if I recall correctly, and correct me if I'm wrong in your testimony - by a mortar round. Did you say something like that in your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to refer you to a document, and this document is at tab number 1 in your report -- in your pile of documents. This is a document which is already in evidence, and I would ask you that you take a look at the document. The first part is a covering letter which is signed by Ambassador Thebault. Now, you know who Ambassador Thebault is. He was the head of the regional centre.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the one you spent the first night with, discussing the situation.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: And then we worked together for three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read what Ambassador Thebault was saying on this first page and confirm whether you agree or not with his assessment of the situation. And I refer you specifically to the second paragraph where it says "if the BiH Army attack is clear, it seems also to be now clear that the allegations of atrocities or ethnic cleansing made by the Bosnian Croats are intentionally exaggerated when not completely false." And then where it says a little further down, that: "In fact, the huge population movements reported are more probably the combined product of the long-lasting HVO propaganda on Muslim-alleged atrocities and the result of clear orders given in certain areas to leave the villages when not to join the Serb lines." Do you recall this assessment by Ambassador Thebault?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly how the discussion was going on. But at this time, I was head on the coordination centre in Travnik that we established during this period. And of course, I had a lot of discussions with Mr. Thebault about the situation in Travnik. And we were, as I remember, very confused about what happened to all these thousands of Croat people that disappeared from Travnik. And I still have no clear picture of what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come, Mr. Junhov, to the issue of the Travnik. But for now, do you recall that the use of propaganda as described by Ambassador Thebault and the use of orders by the HVO authorities to both scare people and get them to leave their villages?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: What I can confirm generally is that there was a lot of rumours and a lot of attempt to scare the people in some purpose. But I don't remember exactly the discussion that led Mr. Thebault to make this special report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer you, Mr. Junhov, to the next document in your binder, in your list of documents. This is a document dated 19th of June. Now, this, of course, is just before you departed for -- at the end of your tour. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer you to the second page of this document where again this is a report that was prepared, the first page, by Jean-Pierre Thebault. And immediately following this report, if you follow me on page 2, is a special report on Travnik dated the 8th of June 1993. Are you with me on the same page?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now refer you to the end of this document on page 5 where it says that the document had been prepared by Philip Watkins and yourself.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall preparing this document?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Date, 8th of June. Okay. What's the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall preparing this document along with Mr. Watkins?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Watkins is the person who came after you as the head of the coordination centre in Travnik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Philip Watkins, if I remember it correctly he was to succeed me when I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I refer you to in terms of the last -- on page -- sorry, on page 4 at paragraph 8 -- yeah, paragraph 8, and it's the fifth line down where it says "the Dolac church has been hit by a single mortar round, and this is not assessed as a deliberate attack." Is that the church that you saw in Dolac that you reported a little earlier?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Where it Dolac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fifth line of paragraph --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: On the map. I have to see a map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer you here to your statement, and where in your statement it is mentioned, and that is on page -- to your statement here it, says "Sometimes in late April, I visited Dolac area, which is located northwest of Zenica. I took a photograph of a destroyed Catholic church." And I just want to ask you whether this church in Dolac is the church that is reported here as having been hit by a single mortar round. If you don't remember, it's not -- it is perfectly okay, Mr. Junhov.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, but I have to have some kind of support for my memory which church is which. And then I would like to see a map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I do not have a map with me.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I have a map in my...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a map, maybe you can take it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Mr. President, and of course if the other side agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Mundis, do you have anything against this line of action?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Witness, would you please have a look at your map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let's see, Dolac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is close to Travnik, northwest of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Is it between Novi Travnik and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, perhaps you could guide the witness. He hasn't got your GPS system.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I can't find the name on the map. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But put the map that you have now in your hands just on the ELMO so that we can all see basically where Dolac is compared to Travnik. Can you use your pencil to point towards Dolac.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Here's Travnik. And Dolac is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where you took the picture of a church that was destroyed and that you later reported as having been destroyed by a single mortar-round hit?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, but the church had also been visited by people who had abused the church. Or if it was like a monastery or like a religious school or something like that. But the church was hit and the inventory of the church was abused. The library was thrown out of the windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to earlier on, Mr. Junhov, to a Catholic church in Travnik. Now, this is two different churches. Right?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first one you reported damage inside which you visited with an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this one you report as having been hit by a mortar round?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, but this church had also been visited by people who destroyed the inventory in the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on to another topic, because it's -- this is -- later on, we will talk about the church in Travnik just to ensure that we are -- to know exactly which church we are talking about. Now, the church you visited in Travnik, the one that had the damage inside --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- this church, you were taken there by a lady who told you that the damage inside had been done by the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the lady also tell you that even though the damage had been done by the Mujahedin, a criminal complaint had been filed and an investigation was underway? Did she tell you that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another issue, and that is the exchange which you referred to in your testimony concerning the foreigners that were detained or at least that were exchanged. My only question I have for you is that of course your information or your knowledge of this exchange is limited to what you saw at the factory; you called it the blue factory.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on this occasion, you mentioned that there was an individual whom you believed to be a Muslim commander.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement, you actually say that you took a picture --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- of this gentleman, and I would like to show you this picture. Do you recall who the gentleman in white is who seems to be a bit taller than the others?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it's Henk Morsink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that he is discussing with the member who you believe to be the Muslim commander?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, and the man with the back is probably an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is you -- you described him in your statement as being a Mujahedin with the beard, wearing a black beret and an Arafat scarf.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was speaking to Mr. Morsink.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the typical Mujahedin you were referring to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like that you sign this picture, please, and put today's date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like to tender the photograph, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, the photograph showing a typical Mujahedin, if I can put it that way. What is your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH191 will be that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Junhov, can you confirm that concerning this exchange, what you recall is that the foreigners were taking into two Warriors that belonged to BritBat and that they were taken to the coast, somewhere in Split?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard. I didn't take part in the transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to a different issue, and that is the issue that you were appointed the head of the coordination centre in Travnik on 1 June. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is you were just returning from 15 days of rest and recreation, known of course as R and R.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: One week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, because in your statement it says that you departed on the 19th and that you came back on the 1st, which made it 15 days. But I agree. To me, if it's one or two weeks, it says 19 May to 2nd of June. Were those dates -- correspond?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, can you confirm with me that the situation you found in Travnik was, to use your own word, chaotic?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that during the first week of June, it was a total war in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: And the area around Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that there was also shelling from the Serbian Army?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that there were great problems; there were lack of food, the roads were blocked, and there was no way to get supplies into the town.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also agree that the town was full of refugees, mostly Muslims, but also Croats?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes. And people who came into Travnik from the west, from the Turbe area and beyond that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that when you arrived being informed that on the 1st of June, the commander of the Operational Group Bosanska Krajina, Mehmet Alagic had been arrested and had been robbed of all of his materiel. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this event where the commander of the operational group is arrested is a significant event that can really contribute to raise tensions to the maximum?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Of course it may contributed to that. But it was one event among a number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I will make my questions more precise. If you arrest one soldier or if you arrest the commander of the operational group, does that make a difference in terms of the impact on the overall situation?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Of course it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that at the same time, the HVO were preventing the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to travel to the front line with the Serbs by establishing some checkpoints? Are you aware of this situation?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That the Croats -- what's the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That the HVO were setting up checkpoints, and that they actually stopped or prevented buses with soldiers from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to travel to the Serb front line. Are you aware of this situation?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember the discussions about that. And of course, from the Croat side then the explanation was that they would like to prevent the BiH forces to cooperate with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you also agree, Mr. Junhov, because -- I mean, I take your assessment of the situation. Do you recall that at that time, the HVO, who up until that time in early June had been keeping the line with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were pulling away from the line, and that created big problems for the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me say that once more. Up until early June --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the front line in Central Bosnia facing the Serbs --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was being held by two armies working together, the HVO on one hand and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, but that was earlier, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, earlier, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay. Then I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree by that time, the HVO had pulled out from the line, thus increasing the burden on the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: From the Croatian side, they might have got that impression. But I don't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yourself, as an observer.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because we were not allowed to go into the area where the Serb Army could have some kind of impact on us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware at that time, Mr. Junhov, that the HVO was actually leaguing up with the Serbs in terms of teaming up together and fighting the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the attack conducted by the HVO on the village of Bandol, which is very close to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Is it east of Travnik or... ?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is going from Travnik. If you look up to the monastery at Guca Gora, then you see the village of -- the village of Bandol is in a line, in a straight line between --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Okay, to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Travnik and Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: And what was the question there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember there was an attack conducted by the HVO on the village of Bandol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just draw to my learned colleague's attention the fact that at line 23 there was no audible response recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will say this question once again, Mr. Junhov. But if you don't remember, just say that you don't remember. I was just referring to because you said that there was total war in Travnik and in the surrounding villages, whether you were aware that the HVO had attacked the village of Bandol. And that actually, every single Muslim house in that village was burnt down. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: The special village of Bandol, I don't remember that exactly. But you see, this was day after day after day with heavy fighting, and I was just in the middle of it sitting in an awful hotel. And what I could see through the windows from the hotel, of course, it limited me. And the few -- it was very hard to get out in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, maybe you can confirm that on the 4th of June you requested to be evacuated from Travnik and taken back to Zenica. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, because I had a number of persons with me, and I was responsible for the security for the people. So I called up the BritBat to come in and evacuate us, which they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on to a different issue, Mr. Junhov, and that is what you referred to as the joint command post or the joint operations centre which was located in the PTT building. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were appointed the senior advisor to this operations centre.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this centre never actually worked out?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the main reasons amongst others was the lack of communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also confirm that Mr. Merdan himself, during that period, was difficult to contact because he was no longer being transported by BritBat and that he had no communications equipment of his own?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I never saw him with any kind of communication equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me move on to a different issue, and that is on the 10th of June, there was a fact-finding mission. And I'd like to refer you to a document in the series of documents that has been given to you, which is at tab 7. And I'd like to refer you to page number 2 where it says that this report has been prepared by yourself and Mr. Watkins.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: If I would have the time to read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take the time to read it, Mr. Junhov, by all means. Do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember it. Yeah, yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that in terms of the route -- I refer you to the middle of the paragraph where we talk about Nova Selo. It says, "The route to the village took us through the Croat village of Nova Selo where there was evidence of fighting but no burnt houses," and that en route to Brajkovici, "Two houses were said to have been destroyed, and one fresh grave was observed. But the houses in the village were intact, without any sign of damage." Do you recall these observations made with Mr. Watkins?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now refer you to another -- moving on to another topic, and that is the Tuzla convoy. Do you remember this convoy?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall that this convoy was, to use your own words, "a total mess," whereas there was actually a military engagement between the UNPROFOR and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that drivers were taken out of their vehicles and killed by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: If it was HVO units or police forces from Vitez, I don't know. But I have photos from many of the trucks with the contents of the brain in the roof of the lorries. They were shot where they sat in the trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that this fighting was done by the HVO or the HVO police?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Or at least with the knowledge of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that even UNPROFOR for the first time killed two persons in self-defence. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I recall the shooting. But if it was the first time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that some trucks were actually taken away and stolen all together, and the convoy was badly looted. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I refer you now to the 14th of June where you actually said something about a house near the centre of Travnik. Now, you said that many houses in Travnik had this sign. I would simply like to confirm that this sign, the reading on this sign, said that "Property under the protection of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina Military Police." Can you confirm that this is what the sign which was on those many houses in Travnik read?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on to a different issue. And that was basically your assessment of the Vance-Owens plan. This is an issue you touched upon with the investigator whom you met. I'd like to refer you to this end to another document which is in your binder, and that is the document at tab number 8. And I would like you to look at paragraph number 3, where it says: "The international community has deployed an increasingly professional humanitarian effort to keep alive the communities isolated by the conflict over the winter of 1992/1993. But their position is now untenable because of the total intransigence of Bosnian Serbs and the Croats in Herzegovina"; and where it says "The final collapse of the infrastructure of Central Bosnia is imminent. However, as the situation within Bosnia-Herzegovina has deteriorated, so the international effort to resolve the conflict has also become disjointed and the way ahead increasingly unclear." Now, do you recall that this is a document that you gave yourself to the investigators of the Tribunal when you met them in 1997?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Who is this -- the author?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The author of this document is the --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Ole Brix-Andersen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is the deputy head of mission, that is, the ECMM in Zagreb. Now, at the end of your statement in 1997, you gave a series of documents to the investigators. This is one of the documents that is on this list. And your comment is "I am providing the Tribunal with several documents which I authenticate. They are true to the best, and I want to attach them to this statement, and I'd like you to consider them to be part of my statement." Do you recall saying this to the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly that, but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document was in the list, and this is a document dated 16th of June.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Which year? 1993, okay. So what's the point?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I simply say whether you recognise this as being one of the documents which you gave to the investigators of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I can't deny that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I go with you to the second page of this document, where it says, talking about the Serbs, that -- at paragraph 6: "The Serbs are contemptuous of the Security Council resolutions and declarations on safe areas and continue to pursue their policy of reducing and removing the Muslim presence in the area as fast as possible." Do you remember reading this document and discussing this document at any point during your stay in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: This is dated the 16th of June. That is the same week that I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you obtained this document while you were in Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer you to this number 10, paragraph number 10 on this page, where it says "the eruption of interethnic violence between Croats and Muslims in Central Bosnia on 16th of April, capped by the atrocity committed in Ahmici, was staged by the Bosnian Croats. They want to start by establishing a secure border between Croat provinces 8 and 10, and the Muslim province number 9." If we go to the next page, "At the same time, they will eliminate all Muslim resistance to their plans within provinces 8 and 10. Once this is achieved, one can expect ethnic cleansing within Croat-controlled areas will be pursued on a far larger scale than is currently possible. This process will probably lead to the securing of independence for the Croatian community within Bosnia and Herzegovina and eventually some sort of formalised relationship with Croatia." And I'd like to refer you just to paragraph 14, because this is where you were in terms of the head of the coordination centre. Are you with me at paragraph 14, sir?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where it says: "Travnik was the only area where the Croat and Muslims appeared to be working well together, despite a number of fights. But on the 4th of June, the Croats evacuated Travnik to Novi Travnik, Vitez, and Turbe held by the Serbs amid allegations of Muslim atrocities. And then it says the Muslims took control first of Travnik and then of the mountain route from Travnik to Zenica." And where it says that "There is evidence that the HVO deliberately withdrew the civilian Croat population from the Travnik area in an attempt to balance their eviction against events in Mostar." Would that be consistent with what you saw as the head of the coordination centre in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, as I mentioned before, we had a lot of discussions about what happens to the Croats in Travnik and who made what. And as I also mentioned before, I didn't get a clear picture of that when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on to a different issue, which is my last issue I would like to cover with you. And that is basically: You mentioned that you met with General Hadzihasanovic. And can you confirm that your assessment of General Hadzihasanovic was that he was professional, educated; that he never raised his voice, that he was polite, and that he behaved correctly at all times?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, I never saw any other behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I tell you information which you might not be aware of, that actually General Hadzihasanovic during his time as commander of the 3rd Corps in Central Bosnia issued a number of directives and orders to his subordinate commanders, to both respect the law, investigate violations, and actually ensure that violations are followed up with disciplinary punishment or even criminal actions, would that be consistent with what you saw of the man in Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, but I am a very realistic person. I see to the result, and not to the speeches and so on. And in my opinion, I think that the commander of Central Bosnia, he was responsible for the area and for what happens there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the commander of the Central Bosnia operative zone, the HVO commander, is responsible for everyone that happened in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: In the area that he controls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They control the same area. So who's responsible?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: They don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're both responsible for the same area. Central Bosnia operative zone and Central Bosnia; do you agree that this is the same area?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Of course, Central Bosnia as a geographic object is the same. But the military control was not overlapping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we agree -- you are a former military officer, and we agree, of course, that in military speaking, we always say that a commander is responsible for everything. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah, that's basic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: If the commander that you met in 1993 issued a number of orders and that these orders led to prosecutions and to a number of people being investigated, being prosecuted, being found guilty, and being sentenced and being put in jail -- now you don't know this information, but if this information was true, I'm just asking you whether this fits in the character of the man that you met called General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I think it's a strange question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can't answer, it's perfectly fine with me. I'm just asking because you met him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, but I never saw such an order as you mentioned. I never saw any actions of courts or sentences and penalties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that you never saw any orders from the 3rd Corps, whether it was to lead an attack, to prepare an attack, --

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to prepare troops, to do any movements. You saw no orders whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then it is normal that you did not see orders for discipline. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just telling you, if it took place, is that consistent with the character of the man that you saw in 1993? And if you cannot answer, it's perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: It's a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me simply move on to the fact that General Hadzihasanovic did mention to you or complain to you that he had no communication equipment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, how much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no another two questions, Mr. President. I'm almost finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And how much time will Mr. Kubura's Defence require?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: We will need 10 minutes to ask a few questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, we will try to conclude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Junhov, can you confirm that General Hadzihasanovic did complain to you that he had problems in communication and that he did not have sufficient equipment and that he did not have any satellite phones? Do you recall this conversation with General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Junhov. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would only like to tender some documents from the bundle into evidence. Perhaps we could do that after my colleague asks his questions. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon. Cross-examined by Mr. Dixon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to return to the topic of damage and destruction. You were shown a report that was prepared by yourself and Mr. Watkins dated 10 June 1993. There's no need to look at it again. Simply, if you could confirm that in that report, following the fact-finding mission, it was found that there was no damage to the village of Brajkovici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember it. But if it's in the report, it's -- of course it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the report - and you can refer to it if you need to - but it's also stated there that there was no damage to the church in Brajkovici, that it was visited and it was completely intact with candles, pictures, et cetera, remaining. Is that something you recall being in the report?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No, I can't remember it. But you have the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it's at tab number 7 of my learned friend's record, if you do wish to refer to it.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on the first page of that report.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: And what was the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That the church was visited in Brajkovici and there was no damage to the church.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, that it says in the report - that's near the bottom of the first page - that the damage to Brajkovici was very limited. Do you agree with me on that point?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition in the report, although Grahovcici was not visited itself, would you confirm that the report notes that this village [Realtime transcript read in error: "church"] was closely observed and also appeared completely intact?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Of course. What is written in the report is what we saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. There was also a TV crew with you on this visit. Do you remember that? A video was made of your mission and what was seen. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: On this special --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That there was a video of your trip and what was observed in Brajkovici and Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: I don't remember that on this special day that there was a television team with us. But we had now and then television teams and also writing journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could correct one matter for the record. At 88.4, it says here "the church was closely observed." But what I in fact said in my question was that the village of Grahovcici was observed and the church was intact. The witness has confirmed that in the report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to refer any longer to the report. I'm moving on now to when you first arrived in April 1993. You mentioned that you were shown an organisational chart of the 3rd Corps in which the 7th Brigade was listed. Would you agree with me that that chart was one prepared by the United Nations based on the information that they knew at the time?
