It wasn't a chart of the Bosnian Army or any of the other warring armies.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No, it was provided by the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You did not have a chart, did you, Mr. Junhov, that was provided by the Army of Bosnia itself setting out which were the units and what the composition of those units were?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know -- even though you didn't have such a chart, did you know at the time that besides the 7th Brigade, there were other manoeuvre units within the 3rd Corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Muslim units or?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Units belonging to the 3rd Corps of the Bosnian Army. Did you know besides the 7th Brigade, that there were other manoeuvre units not attached to a particular territory or area, but moving within the area of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: That is hard to say. Which unit people belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if I mention a few brigades, it might ring a bell. Did you know that the 301 Brigade or 303 Brigade or 314 Brigade or the 17th Krajina Brigade, they were all manoeuvre units able to move with a degree of freedom within the area of 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: It's very hard to identify units. But I have a general impression that they had a constant lack of means and transportation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which units had a constant lack of meanings of transportation?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: All units in...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wouldn't surprise you that there were a number of manoeuvre units operating within the area of the 3rd Corps, would it?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In your testimony in chief, you mentioned that there were certain opinions about which you had no proof. If I could refer to one in particular and ask you whether it is correct that you, in fact, had no juridical proof [Realtime transcript read in error: "group"] that there were groups, as you put it, of foreign fighters which may or may not have been with the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes, the answer is I had no juridical proof of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: But the opinion among the monitors, among the UN personnel, was -- that was this opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as you said in your examination-in-chief, you simply did not have information, did you, about particular individual soldiers and foreigners and which units they may have been with, if within a unit at all?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we move on, I have been alerted to the fact that there's another error on the transcript, and that's at 90, line 8. It's in fact you had no juridical proof, not group. So there was no proof that there were groups in the 7th Brigade. And the answer to that was yes, I had no juridical proof of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question, Mr. Junhov: You never met Mr. Amir Kubura, did you?

utterances.speaker: TORBJORN JUNHOV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no questions for re-examination for the witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, as far as your request to tender documents is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm referring to a series of documents that were shown to the witness. Could documents, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 be tendered into evidence on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, as far as these documents are concerned, they all appear to be official. What would your position be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, we have a number of documents referred to in the list. We have one dated the 15th of April, number 3; the 19th of April, number 4; 21st of April, number 5; the 26th of April, number 6; the 8th of June, number 7; and the 16th of June, that is number 8. Could we have an exhibit number for each of these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the document will be 192. The document RC Zenica will be 193. The document referred to as "the Special Report on Croats in Zenica" will have the number DH198 [as interpreted]. The daily report team document will have the number 195. The daily summary in Travnik will have the number 196. Document Number 8 -- we have a B/C/S version -- a version English, will have the number DH197; and the B/C/S version will have the number 197/B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As the Judges have no questions, Witness, you have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution and by the Defence. The Trial Chamber would like to thank you for having come to testify in The Hague. We wish you all the best. As you are now retired, we wish you all the best in your retirement. We wish you a good trip home. And I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom, and you shouldn't forget to take the bag containing your documents with you. You were very kind and provided these documents to the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll give Mr. Bourgon the floor now who has presented us with four documents. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. These are the four documents that were used with the witness Sir Martin Garrod last Friday. In the list of the documents provided, we first of all have a document. It's a chart prepared by the Defence. There is no date. The second document is a report dated the 2nd of June 1993. Its title is "Special Report, BSA Offensive Action in Central Bosnia." And the third document is dated the 7th of October, and its title is "RC Zenica, Subject: Meeting between DHOM Ops and Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, Commander of 3 BiH Corps, on 4 October 1993." The fourth document, Mr. President, is the first one I used. It has been highlighted -- parts have been highlighted, and I now have a clean copy which I can tender into evidence. And this can replace the one that the Registrar has kept. The date is the 4th of August 1993 and the title is "Human Rights Situation in BiH and Emergency Situation." Could we have four different numbers for these documents, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, as far as these documents are concerned, the ones that were presented at the hearing on Friday and that the Defence couldn't provide in totality, it was necessary to replace one that was highlighted in yellow, that document was dated the 4th of August 1993, and that was the document that had to be replaced, does the Prosecution have any objections to raise to these documents that have been identified and recognised by the witness? Perhaps there's a bundle of documents that the Prosecution could be presented with. Madam Usher, could you please collect the documents in order to refresh the Prosecution's memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have the first three documents. It's the fourth one that I'm a bit -- if I could just be shown the fourth document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fourth document is the one that was placed on the ELMO and parts of it had been highlighted. It was the first document used in the course of the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution has no objection to these four documents being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, we need another four numbers now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the first document, "ECM chart as prepared by Defence team" is DH198. The second one called "special report" will have the number 199, DH199. The other one, the meeting between HOM, will have the number DH200. As far as the last document is concerned, the exhibit will be DH201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It's almost time to adjourn. As I said at the beginning of the afternoon, tomorrow we will broadcast the videotapes, the ones referred to in the document provided to the Judges and the Defence. The Prosecution will state its position before the first video is shown and will respond to the points raised by the Defence, namely the issue of who made the document, when, when it was provided to the Prosecution, et cetera. If the Prosecution isn't in a position to respond to the questions raised, they will inform us of the fact. We need as much information as possible in order to evaluate the reliability of the document. I said the reliability, not it's probative value. So that's how we will proceed. Thank you. And I will see everyone at the hearing tomorrow at 9.00, unless there is something that Mr. Dixon would like to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one additional report, and that is to confirm that the Defence did today file the application with the Blaskic Appeals Chamber in respect of the witness that we discussed at the end of last week. I won't, of course, mention his name. But as we said we would do, that application was filed today, and we will now wait for the ruling from the Appeals Chamber. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that information, which is useful. As I said, I will see you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of June, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
